newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees no sign of U.S. recession right now.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees no sign of U.S. recession right now.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Tuesday he saw no signs of a U.S. recession.
"I don't see any signs of recession right now," he told the House Budget Committee.
He added though that a slowdown at some point was inevitable.
But in putting together its balanced budget plan, the administration assumes that any period of growth below the economy's long-term trend will be offset by growth above that.
Rubin noted that the economy grew "well above trend" in the fourth quarter, when it expanded by 3.9 percent.

In its budget forecast, the administration projects that the unemployment rate will edge up to 5.5 percent next year then hold at that level through 2003. In February, the jobless rate stood at 5.3 percent.
Despite that small increase, Rubin said that the jobs market would remain tight.
